# Pension consolidation

Four old pots from employed years plus my own SIPP. Goal: get down to two at most, one of them the SIPP, without losing anything valuable on the way. Started Sept 2024, mostly done Nov 2024.

## The pots, as found

| Pot | Provider | Value (Sept 2024) | Charges | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KPMG Leeds 2007 to 2011 | Aviva | £23,418 | 0.65% | Group personal pension |
| Lindley & Shaw 2011 to 2016 | Scottish Widows | £31,077 | 0.90% | Had a 12% guaranteed annuity rate? CHECK |
| Lindley & Shaw auto-enrol | NEST | £2,941 | 0.3% + 1.8% contribution charge | |
| Crossgates Housing 2016 to 2019 | Royal London | £18,664 | 0.48% | |
| SIPP (freelance since 2019) | Vanguard | £44,210 | 0.15% platform | Global All Cap |

Total about £120,300. Felt bigger written down than in my head, in a good way.

## Things to check before moving anything

1. **Safeguarded benefits**: guaranteed annuity rates, defined benefit promises, protected tax-free cash above 25%. Any of these and a transfer could throw away something worth far more than the fee saving
2. Exit penalties (old Scottish Widows contracts sometimes have them)
3. Whether the receiving scheme takes the transfer. Vanguard SIPP does, by Origo
4. Lifestyling. Some old default funds de-risk into bonds and cash automatically from age 50. I'm 41, not relevant yet but I want control

## Scottish Widows: the scare

Lindley & Shaw had told us something about a "guaranteed rate" back in 2012. Rang Scottish Widows 2 Oct 2024, call ref SW-PEN-7781. The policy (number 6610392-K) has no GAR, no protected tax-free cash, and no exit penalty. The "guarantee" was a with-profits fund that was closed in 2015 and the money moved to their Pension Portfolio Two. Asked them to confirm in writing; letter arrived 14 Oct. Cleared to transfer.

## Transfers done

- Aviva → Vanguard SIPP: transfer ref **PT-30418**, requested 16 Oct, completed 4 Nov 2024. Out of the market 6 working days because Aviva sold to cash first. Units bought on 4 Nov at a price 0.8% higher than when sold. Cost me ~£190 in effect. Annoying but small.
- Scottish Widows → Vanguard SIPP: ref PT-30422, completed 19 Nov 2024.
- Royal London: **kept**. 0.48% is fine and its fund is a tracker already. Also nice to have more than one provider in case of any admin disaster.
- NEST: tiny, left alone. NEST's contribution charge only applies to new money, and nothing new goes in.

## After

SIPP now ~£99,000. Royal London £18,664. NEST £2,941.

Every transfer, the pension finder service got updated too (gov.uk, checked 22 Nov). The previous address for Aviva was the old flat on Cardigan Road, so the 2021 annual statement went there and the tenant forwarded it, which is how I found out it was still there at all.

## Contributions now

As a sole trader I put in £500 a month gross. Vanguard claims 20% relief at source so I pay £400 net. Higher-rate relief (the extra 20%) has to be claimed on the self assessment, box 1 of the pension section, which I forgot in 2022/23 and had to amend. Details in [[Self assessment 2024]].

Annual allowance £60,000, nowhere near it. Carry-forward available from 3 years if a big invoice year ever happens.

## Open questions

- State pension forecast: £221.20 a week from 2050 with 35 qualifying years. I have 21. Check whether the 2013/14 gap is worth buying back (it's £824 for that year, deadline 5 April 2025). Probably yes.
- Is it worth splitting into a separate bond fund as a pre-retirement buffer? Not until 55. Some of the logic is in [[Bond ladder]].
- Javier's pensions are a completely separate mess in Spain. Not my job, he says. It will be my job.
